message.content: The most recent estimates put the United States’ Gini coefficient at roughly **0.41** (or 41 %) when measured on a pre‑tax, pre‑transfer basis. If you look at the OECD’s “Gini after tax and transfers” figure, it’s a bit lower—about **0.39** (or 39 %). These numbers come from the latest national surveys and international comparisons (OECD, World Bank, U.S. Census Bureau). Keep in mind that the exact figure can vary slightly depending on the methodology and the year of the data used.
